parsed.explanation: The quoted passage is in §3 and the objection reads it correctly: §3 only rules out two distinct *positive* values of g (the argument fixes c_1 > c_2 > 0 and derives a contradiction from (9)). Scanning the whole write-up, the only statement about the sign of g is the parenthetical 'Then g(x) > -x' after (4); no argument anywhere shows g(x) ≥ 0. The standard proof (iterating (4)/(3) to get f^n(x) = x + n g(x) < 0 for large n when g(x) < 0, contradicting positivity of the codomain) is not written. Yet the dichotomy (i)/(ii), the claim '(Because V has only the two values, every x>0 belongs to S_0 ∪ S_c)', and §§4–6 all presuppose V ⊆ {0, c}; if some g(t) < 0 were allowed, the level-set covering argument would not apply. Hence the necessity obligation is incomplete as written.
